question: What may a federation see of its affiliates (member counts, per-capita remittances, meeting records, grievance benchmarks), who in the federation may see it, how is the parent and child relationship between a federation organization and an affiliate established and verified, and what minimum group size suppresses a published grievance statistic?
decision: Affiliation requires independently verified two-sided confirmation and an auditable, revocable data-sharing agreement by authorized offices of both organizations. Share only approved member-count aggregates and remittance obligations with mandated federation finance readers; meeting materials require an item-level grant. Grievance benchmarks use opt-in aggregates, suppress cells below 10 cases and apply residual-identification controls. Parent affiliation alone never grants case or member-record access.
originalProposedDecision: A parent-child link exists only when both orgs' admins confirm it (two-sided handshake, audited). A federation then sees member counts and per-capita remittances owed to it, and meeting records the affiliate shares. Grievance benchmarks are aggregates only, suppressed below 10 cases. Federation readers: its officers and admins. Nothing else without an explicit sharing setting by the affiliate.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
